subject.title: [Bug] Dashboard Stop button can corrupt session files + agent permission isolation lacks guardrails

question: What default boundary should OpenClaw enforce between Dashboard Stop durability and multi-agent host exec authority?
rationale: The source supports a real risk surface, but changing cancellation persistence and host exec defaults affects security posture and existing trusted single-operator workflows, so automation should not choose the product contract alone.

options.title: Split and harden both surfaces
options.body: Keep this issue open as a security/product tracker, first proving Stop durability and then designing per-agent host-exec guardrails with upgrade guidance.

options.title: Fix Stop only for now
options.body: Preserve trusted host exec defaults and narrow the immediate repair to session cancellation durability and JSONL recovery.

options.title: Tighten host exec defaults
options.body: Move default host exec for multi-agent deployments toward approval or sandbox isolation, accepting the need for compatibility proof and migration messaging.

recommendation.title: Split and harden both surfaces
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as a security/product tracker, first proving Stop durability and then designing per-agent host-exec guardrails with upgrade guidance.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter's history covers the exec default policy and a later gateway abort-flow refactor, making him the best available routing owner for the boundary decision.
